summary: Script: runs JavaScript that declares its own typed inputs/outputs, named signal handlers and lifecycle (setup/run/destroy) methods.
description: The Script node executes the JavaScript in its `code` parameter (or, when `useExternalFile` is `yes`, a file fetched from `externalFile`). Unlike the Function node, the script declares its ports explicitly and gets a lifecycle: `define({ inputs: { price: 'number' }, outputs: { total: 'number' }, setup: fn, run: fn, destroy: fn, mySignal: fn })` creates typed input/output ports from the `inputs`/`outputs` maps, runs `setup` once after the code is parsed, runs `run` (alias `change`) each time any value input changes (it receives `(inputs, outputs, changedInputs)`), runs a function named after a signal input when that signal fires, and runs `destroy` when the node is removed. A newer `script({...})` form adds `signals: {}`, `changed: {}` (per-input change handlers) and `methods: {}` sections. Inside handlers, `this.flagOutputDirty(name)` and `this.sendSignalOnOutput(name)` push results out. Typed ports can also be added from the editor panel via the `scriptInputs`/`scriptOutputs` lists.
whenToUse: Use Script when code needs a real lifecycle — initialize a library or subscription in `setup`, tear it down in `destroy` — or several distinct signal entry points with typed ports. For ordinary run-once logic and async calls, prefer JavaScriptFunction (Function): its implicit `Inputs.x`/`Outputs.y` ports and single `run` signal are simpler. For pure one-liners use Expression.

ports.code: The script source (edit-only). Its declared `inputs`/`outputs` maps and signal-handler names define the node's ports.
ports.useExternalFile: Edit-only enum; `yes` swaps the `code` port for `externalFile` and loads the script from a project file at runtime.
ports.externalFile: Edit-only path to a script file; the node stays inert until the file has loaded and parsed.
ports.scriptInputs: Editor-managed list adding typed input ports (with a Type selector per entry) alongside those declared in code.
ports.scriptOutputs: Editor-managed list adding typed output ports alongside those declared in code.

runtimeBehavior: All data and signal ports are runtime-discovered by parsing the script (JavascriptNodeParser): the keys of the declared `inputs`/`outputs` maps become ports with the declared types, each `signals` entry (or top-level handler function named like a signal input) becomes a signal input, and entries in the `scriptInputs`/`scriptOutputs` proplist parameters add further typed ports. Nothing about the port set is static — an authoring tool must write the script first and wire only names the script (or the proplists) declares. Those names are used verbatim: unlike the Function node (`JavaScriptFunction`), whose mined ports are named `in-x` / `out-y`, the Script node adds no prefix, so a declared input `price` is wired as `toProperty: "price"`. When `useExternalFile` is `yes` the ports come from the downloaded file, so they are unknowable until it loads.
patterns: Wrap a stateful browser library: instantiate it in `setup`, feed it from `changed` handlers, dispose it in `destroy`.
Declare `mySignal: function (inputs, outputs) {...}` and wire a Button `onClick` to the `mySignal` input for an explicit, named action entry point.
antiPatterns: Using Script for a simple transform that reruns on input change — the Function node does that with less ceremony.
Assigning outputs without the declared `outputs` entry: undeclared names never become ports.
